sections.MESSAGE_TO_USER:
mboetger approved [#196561](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561) ("Overall LGTM."), but a few minutes earlier he left 3 inline comments. Nobody has answered them yet. He is a human reviewer, so no agent will reply on GitHub. I'll draft the replies for you to post.

**Comment 1** ([r4606831206](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561#discussion_r4606831206)), "nit: toBigIntegerOrNull() exists": he is right that Kotlin has `String.toBigIntegerOrNull()`. It would replace the `try`/`catch` around `BigInteger(value)`. This is cosmetic. It is worth doing only if it rides along with another push, and only after the worker confirms it gives the same results (sign, whitespace and empty input).

**Comments 2–3** ([r4606860038](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561#discussion_r4606860038)): this one is not a nit. He says the KDoc on `errorMessage` is wrong. In his test, an APK with no `versionCode` installed fine with `adb`. Only Play Store upload fails, and so does installing over a build that has a `versionCode`. The KDoc's claim is the stated reason the error message does not suggest `-P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true`. If he is right, two things follow:
- The KDoc is factually wrong, and the error would ship that way into 3.50 and 3.51.
- The decision to leave the flag out of the error may also be wrong, since the flag does help local `adb` testing. That would change the user-facing message, not only a comment.

We have not reproduced his claim yet. His account is plausible: Android treats a missing `versionCode` as 0, which installs fresh but fails as a downgrade. I won't call it a doc-only fix until it is reproduced. I've asked matt561 to reproduce it on an emulator and to prepare any change locally **without pushing**. Pushing dismisses all 3 approvals and reruns about an hour of presubmits, so nothing moves until you decide the question below.

**Decision 1: merge now, or hold for one batched push?**
- **1a (recommended): hold the merge until the reproduction comes back, then make one push.** That push holds the nit, the KDoc fix and any error-message change the result calls for. Cost: about an hour of presubmits plus fresh approvals from you, bkonyi and mboetger, so the cherry-picks slip by part of a day. Benefit: 3.50 and 3.51 each get one correct cherry-pick, not two. Before calling the PR ready again, I'd run `adversarial-review` on the fix diff.
- **1b: merge now and fix it in a follow-up PR.** Cherry-picks can start today. But the wrong reasoning, and maybe the wrong user-facing message, lands in main. If the follow-up changes behavior, you'd need a second cherry-pick for each branch.
- **1c: merge now and drop comments 2–3.** I don't recommend this before the reproduction. His claim is a behavior report, not a style point.

Reply "go 1a" to hold, or "go 1b" to merge now and follow up.

Draft replies for you to post (I'll finalize them after the reproduction):
- Comment 1: "Done, switched to `toBigIntegerOrNull()`." (Only if we push.)
- Comments 2–3: I'll draft this once matt561 reports, quoting the exact install results.
sections.WORKER_BRIEF:
<WORKER-BRIEF>

- **Source:** Three inline comments on flutter/flutter#196561 from `mboetger`, a human reviewer. He posted them just before approving with "Overall LGTM."
  1. https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561#discussion_r4606831206, `ManifestVersionCodeTaskHelper.kt` line 113, on the `try { BigInteger(value) } catch (e: NumberFormatException) { null }` block:
     > nit: toBigIntegerOrNull() exists
  2. https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561#discussion_r4606860038, `ManifestVersionCodeTaskHelper.kt` line 152, on the KDoc for `errorMessage(variantName, reason)`. That KDoc says: "When the manifest has no positive `versionCode`, the flag builds APKs with no `versionCode`, which Android refuses to install."
     > I don't think this is true.  Can't submit to Play Store sure - but I was able to install with adb.

     Then, in the same thread:
     > I believe it will reject if you try to install over a build with a versionCode.

- **Claims and evidence:**
  - "An APK with no `versionCode` installs with adb": mboetger's report. **We have not reproduced it.**
  - "Installing it over a build with a `versionCode` is rejected": mboetger's belief. **We have not reproduced it.**
  - "Play Store rejects it": mboetger's statement. We can't test this locally. Treat it as his claim.
  - "`toBigIntegerOrNull()` behaves the same as the `BigInteger(value)` try/catch": **not verified.**

- **Task:**
  1. Reproduce comments 2–3 before changing anything. Use a test app whose `android {}` block omits `versionCode` and whose main manifest has no positive `versionCode`. Build with `flutter build apk --split-per-abi -P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true`. For each case, record the exact command and its output, and note the emulator or device API level:
     - `aapt2 dump badging` (or an equivalent tool) on a built APK, showing what `versionCode`, if any, ends up in it.
     - `adb uninstall <pkg>`, then `adb install <apk>` on a clean device.
     - Install a build of the same app that has a positive `versionCode`, then try `adb install` (and `adb install -r`) with the no-`versionCode` APK over it.
     - If the code treats a manifest `versionCode` of `0` or a negative number differently from a missing one, repeat the steps for that case.
  2. Based on the results, tell me whether code, tests or docs must change. The KDoc reasoning may be wrong. If so, say whether the user-facing error message should now mention `force-version-code-ignoring-abi`, for example for local `adb` installs, with its Play Store and upgrade caveats. Or say whether only the KDoc needs fixing. Explain your reasoning; don't just follow the comment.
  3. For comment 1, check whether `toBigIntegerOrNull()` matches the current behavior for leading `+` or `-`, whitespace, empty strings and non-ASCII digits. If it does, prepare the change. If it doesn't, explain why we should decline it.
  4. Make all changes as **local commits only**, based on the current head `f3d2ab1fd3b`. Run the relevant Gradle and unit tests locally and report the commands and results.

- **Constraints:**
  - Branch `vcfix-manifest-fallback` on the `reidbaker-agent` fork, head `f3d2ab1fd3b`.
  - **Do not push.** A push dismisses three approvals and reruns about an hour of presubmits. The user is deciding whether to batch fixes or merge as-is, and I'll tell you when to push.
  - Scope is only these three comments. No other edits, rebases or cleanups.
  - mboetger is a human reviewer. **Do not post or resolve anything on GitHub.** Put a draft reply for each thread in your report, stating what changed or why we decline it, with the reproduction results.
  - Report: the reproduction commands and outputs, your recommendation for each comment (change, modify or decline), the local commit SHAs, and the `git diff f3d2ab1fd3b..HEAD` summary.
